title: Excellence Is Not a Performance Target
author: Kevin Estes
summary: Estes distinguishes between excellence as a standard of work versus excellence as an outcome, arguing that treating excellence as a performance target distorts behavior, erodes discipline, and deteriorates decision-making. Drawing on research and coaching wisdom, he shows how focusing on processes and standards—rather than outcomes—produces superior long-term results and maintains performance under pressure.
points: Excellence describes a standard for achieving the work, not the outcome itself; confusing these produces counterproductive behavior.
When leaders fixate on outcomes, decision-making quality deteriorates under pressure, tension builds, and hesitation compromises performance.
Excellence is a way of working with attention to detail, prideful ownership, and continuous improvement—not a box to check.
Top coaches teach athletes to view excellence as process-based, not outcome-based; the same principle applies to leaders and teams.
quotes: People hit targets and achieve goals all the time without doing excellent work. That's because excellence describes a standard for achieving the work, not the outcome.
When excellence becomes a performance target, it distorts behavior. Emotions take over. Decision-making becomes cloudy.
Excellence is a standard people constantly pursue, not a box that can be checked.” Archived from Admired Leadership on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
